fullPassage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater (a) accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they (b) include information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the (c) quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is (d) morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to (e) escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.

det.korean: (A) 이 숫자들은 그들이 다닌 학교의 질을 설명하지 못한다. (B) 그녀는 대학 등록금을 모으기 위해 새 은행 계좌를 열었다.
det.analysis:

✅ ② (A) 설명하다 — (B) 계좌: (A)에서 account for는 '~을 설명하다/~을 차지하다'라는 숙어이고, (B)에서 account는 '계좌'라는 명사이다.
❌ ③ (B)는 은행과 관련된 맥락이므로 '보고서'가 아니라 '계좌'가 적절하다.
❌ ④ (A)는 'account for' 구동사로 '설명하다'이며, '보고서'가 아니다.
det.tip: account는 다의어입니다. ① 계좌(bank account) ② 설명(account for) ③ 보고서/이야기(give an account of). 'account for'는 '~을 설명하다, ~을 차지하다'라는 중요한 숙어입니다.

❌ ④ statistics(통계): 수집된 데이터를 분석하는 학문/결과이지 조사 행위 자체가 아니다.
